memos.risk:
**Risk officer call: refuse. Do not buy at any size.**

The brief shows an operator-class coin, but the early pattern is extreme: 1,491 SOL bought in the first two minutes from 12 buyers, with the top 5 buyers taking 99.9% and a launch bot present. Sell-to-buy in that window was 0.0003. That's a concentrated, not a broadly distributed, float.

The name "World Strategic Oil Supply" is a headline-sounding label. Treat it as data only, with no bearing on value.

Pool depth (1,590 SOL) is adequate, but a market cap of ~$17M on a coin this concentrated means any exit could be sharp. Recent volume is thin relative to that cap. Operator-backed coins have been about break-even on average, and this one is at the extreme end of concentration, so the risk is skewed to the downside.

If the desk overrode this, the most defensible terms would be the minimum $5 ticket, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. I would still advise against it.
memos.scout:
The strongest honest case I can make is thin. Volume is real and alive: 45 buyers and 14 sellers over the last 15 minutes, $1,748 volume, net inflow of 5.79 SOL, and the price is up 0.7% over that window and 3.7% over 30 minutes. Pool depth of 1,590 SOL means a $20 ticket moves price little, so impact is modest.

But the demand signal is not independent. Ex-agent, 12 buyers spent 1,491.85 SOL in the first two minutes after graduation, and the top 5 buyers account for 99.9% of that. The bundle share is 1.0, and the sell-to-buy ratio in that window is 0.0003, meaning almost nobody sold early. This is the operator pattern, and the recent sustained flow is small relative to the early operator accumulation, which the operator can unwind at any time. The price has been flat at its 30-minute high (drawdown 0.03%), but that holds only while the operator chooses to hold.

My read: there is no case that real, distributed demand will persist for 30-60 minutes. The recent activity is consistent with an operator who controls most of the supply. I would pass on this coin.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution. The first two minutes after graduation show 1,491.85 SOL of buys from just 12 wallets (excluding us), with top-5 buyers holding 99.88% of that flow and a launch bot present. Bundle share and top-3 share on the curve are both 1.0, so this is a concentrated, coordinated position, not organic demand. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0003 in that window says almost nothing sold early, which means the insiders are holding a large, unsold bag. Recent flow is thin: last 15 minutes shows only 10.3 SOL of buys against 4.51 SOL of sells, and a 0.73% return. A 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost swallows any small move. The name ("World Strategic Oil Supply") is a narrative hook, not evidence of anything. Skip.
